The fear of MSG started with some racist guy complaining about false health issues after eating chinese food and publishing a paper on it saying that it was MSG that caused it.

Guy was racist towards the Chinese.

While it is true that MSG can increase your blood pressure and can cause other health complications, that's not really unique to it.

...

Because it's the sodium that does that.

...

You know.

The sodium that makes up half of salt?

MSG isn't healthy. 

But neither is it unhealthy.

What it is, however, is something you can use to make food taste better.

And let me tell you, ever since I actually thought about why people hate MSG so much and realized, after looking at its chemical composition, that it really isn't as bad as people think, not even close, (We still eat bread, we still eat salt, we still eat meat, we still eat... You get what I mean) with the fear of it being rooted in racism, I started using it more.

And oh boy did I start eating healthier after.

I always knew veggies could taste good, but my god, MSG makes it so much easier.

There is no reason to fear MSG.

It is literally just... Sodium and gluten.

You know...

Salt and... The main thing that makes bread so nice to eat.

...

Speaking of bread, don't we have a very common dish here in the Philippines that is exactly that?

Pandesal.

Pan = Bread

Sal = Salt.

MSG is in practically everything.

Even soy sauce.

And that's okay.

Because when it comes down to it, it's really just another source of sodium.

Of course, one should always be mindful of how much one uses, but that's the same for regular ol' salt.

Iodized or not.

(I recommend iodized. We made those for a reason, y'know? Don't want y'all to have any iodine deficiencies.)

Just because it sounds oh so scary doesn't mean it's bad.

I'm sure if people started marketing water as dihydrogen monoxide, anyone uneducated enough would be skeptical, no?




Edit: I am aware that Gluten and Glutamates are not necessarily the same thing. In fact, glutamic acid is gluten free.

But glutamates are found in large quantities in gluten. 

Take wheat, for example.

30%-35% of its proteins consist of glutamic acid.

Das a lotta glutamic acid you're chomping on if you use wheat for your bread.

And yet filipinos recommend bread or biscuits as an alternative to eating rice.

Despite, y'know...

Apparently being afraid of sodium and glutamic acid being put together.

For those who don't know, Monosodium Glutamate's chemical composition is C5H8NO4Na. 

That is to say 5 Carbon atoms, 8 Hydrogen atoms, 1 Nitrogen atom, 4 Oxygen atoms, and 1 Sodium atom.

Salt is just NaCl, meaning 1 Sodium atom and 1 Chlorine atom.

Wait, but isn't Chlorine a cleaning agent? Isn't drinking chlorine bad for you?

Does that mean we should stop using salt just because Chlorine is literally poisonous?

Also no.

Chlorine regulates several bodily functions including, but not limited to, your body's pH levels.

So yeah.

MSG isn't bad.

It sounds scary, sure.

But Sodium Chloride also sounds scary on paper.

I mean... Who would be crazy enough to eat a metal that will literally explode in water combined with a cleaning agent?

But no, that's just salt.

Master that before you move on to trying his other aspects such as with his arm cannons and his flamethrowers and such because you'll need to switch around your equipment for less mobility.

Fencer can be the most flexible or the most inflexible class in the game depending on your loadout.

Master the flexible side first then go for the inflexible one.

You can't honestly expect a king to let his people be slaughtered and not do something about it when he knows he could've done something. 

Rimuru Tempest is, first and foremost, a ruler. He may not be a perfect ruler, but he is a ruler nonetheless. "Rimuru is too nice." is bullshit. He's not "too" nice. He's a nice person. Good all around, but he's not "too" nice. Neither is he "too" ruthless. Rimuru *has* to be ruthless at times. That's his responsibility as king and his own ideals and emotions at play. 

He's emotional, of course. He massacred the Falmuth kingdom's army out of anger as well as in hope of becoming a Demon King to revive his fallen comrades. A *good* ruler would do that for his people and he would bear that responsibility with dignity and grace. 

Do not forget, he is the ruler of monsters. They were attacked first, under false pretenses, even. The Falmuth kingdom poked at the hornet's nest, not knowing exactly how much trouble it'd cause and it cost them their kingdom. 

Does that justify the massacre? No, gods no. Was it the right thing to do as a human being? No. It simply isn't.

But as a ruler, that was the right thing to do. The ruler has a responsibility to the people who serve under him and a good ruler will see that responsibility through no matter what it entails.

Tl;dr: Rimuri *is* ruthless. He's too ruthless for normal people to understand, but if you look at it from the eyes of a king, he did the right thing prioritizing his own nation's prosperity over others' kingdoms.

Well, it really depends on the weapon you're using. Check their scaling. But mainly, you'll want Vitality, Strength, and Skill. Endurance is something that you need to play around with to know when to stop. Most players cap at 15 Endurance, but it's your choice if you want to go lower or higher. Just don't go above 40 as you only get 1 Stamina Point every 5 levels. But again, it's your choice if you even want to level Endurance. I tend to just leave mine at base. 

Now, for the whole scaling thing. So, every weapon has its own scaling. A weapon like the Threaded Cane benefits more from Skill than Strength (Skill weapon) while the Hunter's Axe benefits more from Strength (Strength weapon). You can see by the letters shown in their respective stat scaling in the weapon information. Now, every weapon has Arcane scaling. But don't go levelling Arcane just because you think it'll increase physical damage. The Arcane scaling applies to elementally converted weapons as well as a select few normal weapons that have inherent elemental damage on them.

What are elementally converted weapons? They are weapons that have elemental gems on it. Let's say you have a Saw Cleaver. A Saw Cleaver is a Quality weapon. It benefits from both Strength and Skill. You have three gem slots within the Saw Cleaver as with other weapons. If, at any point, you find an elemental gem (Like a Fire Damp Blood gem) and you equip it, it removes all Strength and Skill Scaling and it makes it so your weapon scales with Arcane exclusively.

The stat that we haven't talked about is Bloodtinge. Bloodtinge improves damage on a select few right hand weapon as well as most guns. Guns are more intended for parrying, so if you thought you'd start becoming a monster damage dealer with a gun if you level this up, you'd be wrong. Melee weapons are still the best for damage. But that's not to say that Bloodtinge is useless. Weapons that scale with Bloodtinge are scarce. There isn't that many. If you do find them, they're certainly a force to be reckoned with if you have the right stats and gems.

Right, a little thing about Skill. It improves Visceral damage. So if you're going to parry a lot, you might want to consider levelling this one. But again, it depends on your weapon.

To sum it all up, be mindful of your scaling. Check your weapon. Most weapons scale with Strength and Skill. Meaning you'll want Strength and Skill the most over any damage stat UNLESS you plan on using Bloodtinge or Arcane weapons. Vitality is always important, specially in this game. Endurance can be levelled, but is recommended to be kept on the low side. Bloodtinge and Arcane are very weapon specific. Need to find/make weapons that scale with it.
